title: Show the trade between risk and NPV

expected.says: Run's report for the demo export matches the expected report

blueprint.signature: def best(request: Request, first: str, floor: float | None = None) -> Plan
blueprint.contract: Maximizes the goal named first ('npv' or 'risk'), with an optional floor on the risk removed as a row named risk_floor; then, holding the first goal at its best within KEEP, maximizes the other. Returns the second solve's Plan, or the first one's when it is not optimal.
blueprint.idea: A lexicographic second solve keeps the first goal and takes the most of the other, so no point is beaten by a plan equal on the first goal.

blueprint.signature: def dominates(a: Point, b: Point) -> bool
blueprint.contract: True when point a is at least as good as b on both goals and better on one, each comparison within the slack KEEP gives that goal.
blueprint.idea: A point is on the frontier when no other point dominates it.

blueprint.signature: def frontier(request: Request, points: int = 5) -> list[Point]
blueprint.contract: Returns up to `points` non-dominated points, from the best NPV to the most risk removed: the two ends, then best NPV for risk floors spread evenly between the ends' risk. Drops a point whose NPV repeats one already found, and any dominated point. Empty when either end is not optimal.
blueprint.idea: The epsilon-constraint method: maximize one goal while the other must reach a floor, for a series of floors.

blueprint.contract: Adds a row risk_floor (the plan removes at least the request's risk_floor) when the request sets one, and nothing otherwise.
blueprint.idea: A floor the planners set is one more named row over the risk expression.

blueprint.contract: Solves a Built the caller may have changed after build (a new objective, an extra row) and returns its Plan.
blueprint.idea: Solving a model you changed is a separate step from building it.

blueprint.contract: Sets the NPV and risk expressions on the Built before the rules run, so a rule may name them.
blueprint.idea: A rule over a goal needs the goal's expression to exist first.

blueprint.contract: Also reads the request's optional risk_floor, in $k; None when the export has none.
blueprint.idea: The floor is a request setting, so the planners can ask for it in the export.

cases: the frontier runs from the best NPV to the most risk removed
the frontier finds the plan between its two ends
no frontier point is beaten on both goals by another
of two plans tied on NPV, the frontier's NPV end is the one removing more risk
a risk floor in the export gives the best NPV above that floor
